description: Known-answer benchmark for the LIES qmd read surface. Twelve-plus queries spanning five collections, two of them multi-collection and one a deliberate paraphrase. Regenerate with tools/qmd_bench_fixture.py; every expected path is verified against the live index, never guessed.

queries.description: Hook event names and matcher regex in the hooks config.
Filesystem and network allow/deny rules for the sandbox.
Running a delegated subagent and collecting its result.
Multi-agent team layout, distinct from plain subagents.

queries.query: the conversation keeps growing until it no longer fits; what happens then?
queries.description: Paraphrase case: the wording shares no vocabulary with the document (no 'context', 'window', or 'compact'). Neither BM25 nor the reranked pipeline matches it; only the vector and hybrid backends do, which is what makes the hyde / paraphrase-count question measurable.
Sequence diagram syntax: participants, messages, activation.
Gantt chart sections, dateFormat, and excludes.
Flowchart node shapes, subgraphs, and edge direction.
Class diagram relations and cardinality markers.
Declaring tools and their structured output schema.
Server context, dependency injection, and middleware.

typer parameters. Rank 1 under BM25 scoped to typer, but falls out of the unscoped BM25 top 10 that qmd bench uses (ftsLimit = limit when no collection filter is set), so only the vector/hybrid backends match it. Retained because a collection-scoped keyword search that the unscoped one loses is exactly the behaviour the routing change touches.
typer's FileText / FileBinaryRead family. Reachable by all four backends.

queries.query: ask before running shell commands allow block ordered rules
queries.description: Multi-collection: both corpora document ordered shell-permission rules (claude_code/permissions.md and opencode/v2/docs/permissions.md both match this query). Scoping to one collection starves the other.

queries.query: define a custom command that expands to a prompt
queries.description: Multi-collection: user-defined slash commands in both corpora.

qmd_bench.latency_note: Observed once, at the time of recording. NOT A GATE: three runs against an unchanged index gave bit-identical quality metrics and 10x-different latency (cold vs warm embedding/reranker models). Compare the quality metrics; ignore this. The 2026-10-02 re-measurement was taken with a COLD model cache (the llm_cache had just been cleared), so its vector/hybrid/full latencies are cold figures and must not be compared against a warm baseline.

stability.method: Run twice back to back with `qmd bench tests/fixtures/qmd_bench.json --json` and compare every quality metric. This is the Task 1 method: three runs against an unchanged index gave bit-identical quality.

recorded_against.note: 1601 orphan hashes and 42086 orphan rows, against the same 5987 documents. The reconciliation is exact and arithmetic: 42086 orphan rows removed, 91070 - 42086 = 48984, which is the recorded post-cleanup vector count. The ~26 vectors per orphan hash is simply what 1601 deleted documents' chunks look like. Nothing was re-chunked: every surviving document kept its vectors.

superseded_baseline.why_replaced: These numbers cannot be reproduced by the current index and must not be gated against. Superseded on 2026-10-02, NOT because a code change moved them, and not because the index was re-chunked. Two findings, both verified: (1) `qmd bench` runs in-process -- `dist/cli/qmd.js` `case "bench"` imports `../bench/bench.js` directly, which has no daemon, no MCP server and no subprocess, so no LIES code is on the path at all; every change this branch makes is in LIES. (2) The index changed underneath the gate. The old figures were measured at 91070 vectors and 1566 orphan hashes; the index is now 48984 vectors with 0 orphans and 0 documents lacking vectors (all 14 collections fully covered). The cleanup deleted only rows with no backing `content`, i.e. exactly the orphans: 42086 orphan rows against 91070 vectors leaves 48984, the recorded post-cleanup count, and every one of the 5987 surviving documents still has vectors. Nothing was re-chunked and no document lost coverage. See `recorded_against` for the arithmetic. The delta is environmental.

which_queries_moved.note: Two reranker-sensitive queries account for the whole delta: `cc-context-window-paraphrase` (semantic) and `fm-server-context` (topical) now score 0 recall. Both expected files are still present, active and vectorised, so this is ranking, not missing documents.

index_state_at_recording.note: The index state this block was measured against, so the count is checkable rather than asserted. Every one of the 5987 active documents has vectors; 0 documents lack them.

baseline.lies_gate_note: Not filled by qmd bench. That summary measures qmd's own four backends in-process (no daemon, no per-query collection scope, no LIES ground() fan-out), so no LIES routing change can move it. This slot measures LIES as it actually routes, and is therefore the only place the multi-collection starvation signal can land: the two multi-collection queries below are inert in the qmd_bench numbers, because the harness takes one global -c and never exercises per-query scope. Record here: corpus_documents, qmd_version, method, queries_total, queries_passing. ADDED 2026-10-02: a qmd_bench number moved once and no LIES change was behind it. `qmd bench` runs in-process (dist/cli/qmd.js `case "bench"` imports ../bench/bench.js, which has no daemon, no MCP server and no subprocess), so every change this branch makes is provably off its path. The index changed instead: 1566 orphan hashes -> 0 and 91070 -> 48984 vectors, across the same 5987 documents, all of them still vectorised. The qmd_bench block was re-recorded against that index and verified reproducible (two runs, every quality metric bit-identical); the superseded figures and the index state they belong to are kept in `qmd_bench.superseded_baseline`. The lesson for whoever reads the next delta: a change here means the index or qmd moved, and only a change in the slot below means LIES moved.
